engineMetrics.unreadable: The engine published nothing this build could read.
engineMetrics.heading: Engine metrics
engineMetrics.oneSample: One sample so far — a second is needed before a rate or a line exists.
engineMetrics.runningHint: Requests the engine is decoding right now.
engineMetrics.queuedHint: Requests accepted but not yet running. A deep queue is the clearest sign the model is saturated.
engineMetrics.kvCacheHint: How full the KV cache is. Near 100% the engine starts preempting.
engineMetrics.preemptionsHint: Requests evicted and restarted since the engine last started. Cumulative, not a rate.

counterResets.one: The engine's counters restarted {count} time in this window. Token rates across those intervals are unknown rather than zero, so the lines break there.
counterResets.other: The engine's counters restarted {count} times in this window. Token rates across those intervals are unknown rather than zero, so the lines break there.

engineMetrics.volatileCaption: Read from the engine's own /metrics endpoint and held in the control plane's memory only. Restarting Spark Pulse loses this window; nothing here is written to disk.
engineMetrics.noPercentiles: Latency percentiles are not shown: both engines publish histograms and no pre-computed percentile, so an honest p95 needs Prometheus querying this same endpoint.

nodes.heading: Nodes
nodes.subtitle: The nodes this control plane knows about. Each keeps a minted identity, so renaming or re-addressing one does not re-enroll it.
nodes.name: Name
nodes.sshUserPlaceholder: The account with sudo on the node
nodes.mdnsUnavailable: mDNS is unavailable here, so nothing can be discovered. Type the address above instead — that always works.
nodes.noResponders: No responders answered. Type the address above instead.
nodes.forgetBody: Forget "{name}"? This drops what we know about the node. It does not touch the node itself — uninstalling an agent and wiping a node's identity are separate actions.
nodes.addNote: Adding registers the node. Installing the agent on it is the next step, and it starts as soon as this is added.

edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.controlPlaneNote: The control plane is reached over its own agent, not an address other nodes dial it at, so only its name can be changed here.

install.title: Install the agent on {name}
install.intro: SSH carries the agent onto {address} once. After that the node dials the control plane and SSH is not used for it again.
install.passwordNote: Used once to place the control plane's key on the node, which is then verified without it. The password is not stored.
install.keyPlaceholder: Paste the key, or upload the file below
install.keyNote: Unlocked on the control plane and used to log in from there. The key is not sent to the node and not stored.
install.passphraseNote: Only if the key is encrypted.
install.controlPlaneKeyNote: For a node whose authorized_keys already holds this control plane's public key — a reinstall, or a key you copied by hand.
install.sudoNote: Used only if the node needs something elevated, such as enabling lingering or a system unit. Leave blank for passwordless sudo.
install.checking: Asking the node for its host key…
install.hostKeyHint: Compare it with what the node prints for {command}. Nothing has been sent to it yet.
install.runHint: Enabled once the host key has been checked.
install.running: Copying the agent, enrolling it and waiting for it to dial home. This takes a while.
install.notConnected: Installed, but the agent has not dialled home yet.
install.updateHint: This node runs agent {version}; this control plane ships {current}. Reinstalling keeps the node's identity and only replaces the binary. The control plane's key is already on the node, so no password is needed.

doctor.healthy: Nothing wrong that the doctor can see.
doctor.sudoNote: Only if a repair needs root, such as adding the docker group. Kept nowhere.

nodes.hostKeyFailed: Could not read the host key

deployOptions.extraArgsNote: Appended to the engine command, quoted.
deployOptions.heading: Deploy options
deployOptions.modelPlaceholder: leave empty for the recipe's model
deployOptions.noImagePublished: no image has been published for this engine yet
deployOptions.commandPinsVllm: recipe carries an engine-specific command for 'vllm'
deployOptions.imageMissing: image not pulled, {size} will download first
deployOptions.modelMissing: not downloaded — Deploy will offer to fetch it
deployOptions.sourceCache: the model cache on the node
deployOptions.sourceEngineDownload: the engine fetches its own copy
deployOptions.occupancyTooMany: {flags} does not fit {nodes}: it needs {needed}. This hardware has one GPU per node, so either lower the parallelism or deploy across {needs}.
deployOptions.occupancyTooFew: {flags} only occupies {needed} of the {nodes} selected. One GPU per node means the world size is the node count, so the extra {spare} would join the rendezvous with nothing to hold, and vLLM refuses a --nnodes that does not divide it exactly, so this would fail on every rank rather than serve on a subset. Deploy on {needs}, or raise the parallelism until tp*pp is {count}.

newRecipe.name: Recipe name

newRecipe.formatsNote: Both recipe formats are accepted. Validation reports each problem against the field it belongs to.

settings.authOff: This API answers every caller that can reach it. The browser boundary is the origin check.
settings.benchmarkingHelp: Show the Benchmarking page and its API.
settings.cacheDirsHelp: One per line. Mounted into every container, so a compiled kernel survives the container that built it — the difference between a warm start and several minutes of recompilation.
settings.clusterModeHelp: Forces recipes that need more than one node on. They are offered anyway once a second node is enrolled, so this is for a cluster still being built.
settings.discoveryIdle: Detects this node's interfaces and the NCCL defaults they imply. Reports only — nothing is saved.
settings.externalUrlHelp: Pins the OIDC redirect. Empty means it is worked out from the request, which trusts the Host header.
settings.featuresHelp: Switches that change what this control plane offers, not how a run behaves. Turning one off removes its page and its route.
settings.hfHelp: Passed as HF_TOKEN when launching a run and used to fetch gated models. Stored in ~/.config/spark-pulse/secrets.json; it is never sent back to this page.
settings.imageRegistryLocal: A full registry on this node. Worker nodes pull from here rather than from the internet.
settings.imageRegistryProxy: Pull-through cache of {upstream}. Worker nodes pull from here rather than from the internet.
settings.keepEntrypointHelp: Off means the launch script runs as PID 1, which is what puts the engine's output in the run log.
settings.limitsHelp: Applied on top of the engine's own profile, so a value here overrides what the engine asked for. Leave a limit empty to let the engine decide.
settings.mcpFeatureHelp: Lets an MCP client drive this control plane. Set in the environment, so it is shown here rather than switched.
settings.mcpHelp: Model Context Protocol, on this same app and behind the same auth.
settings.memLimitHelp: Empty means no limit — which is not the same as a limit of zero.
settings.modAllow: Allow — mods may reach the network
settings.modDeny: Deny — refuse a mod that reaches out
settings.modPolicyHelp: A mod is a shell script that runs inside the container before the engine starts. One that downloads something is installing code nobody reviewed.
settings.ncclNote: Detected on this node. Interface pinning is per node, not global: record these on the node's entry in the Fleet page's registry, which is what a deploy reads.
settings.originsHelp: Browser origins that may call this API. Never a wildcard.
settings.portRangeHelp: A run that does not ask for a port is given a free one from this range.
settings.privilegedHelp: Full host access. The GPU devices need it; nothing else here does.
settings.pullTimeoutHelp: A pull making no progress for this long is abandoned rather than left hanging. Measured from the last byte, not from the start.
settings.readyTimeoutHelp: How long a run may take to answer its readiness probe before it is called failed. A large model loading from cold disk is slow.
settings.retentionHelp: Stopped and failed runs older than this are removed automatically. 0 = keep forever.
settings.runtimeNote: How this process is configured. Read-only here on purpose: these are set in settings.json or the environment, and a browser that could change them would be a way past every other check.
settings.stateStoreHelp: Runs, nodes, sessions and the enrolment ledger.
settings.swapLimitHelp: Total of memory and swap. Set it equal to the memory limit to forbid swapping.
settings.title: Settings
settings.webuiPortEnv: Controlled by the WEBUI_PORT environment variable.
settings.workerThreadsHelp: Blocking work is offloaded here rather than run on the event loop.
settings.agentAutoUpdateHelp: Keep each node's agent on the version this control plane ships. A node running an older binary is updated over its own stream, no SSH. On by default.
settings.heading: Settings.

fabric.noTransport: The agent transport is not running, so no node's ports are known.

fabric.override: Re-address nodes that are already configured
fabric.sudoNote: Writing /etc/netplan and applying it needs root on each node. Used for this call and kept nowhere; leave blank for passwordless sudo.
fabric.applying: Writing the files, applying them and reading each port back…
fabric.modeDual: Both cables between two nodes: one subnet pair per cable, no mesh settings.

settingsPage.subtitle: One form; Save writes everything.
settingsPage.shmHelp: /dev/shm. Tensor-parallel workers pass tensors through it; too small shows up as a hang, not an error.
settingsPage.pidsHelp: Processes and threads a container may hold. An engine with many workers needs more than the Docker default.
settingsPage.nofileHelp: Open file descriptors a container may hold. A large model is thousands of shards.
settingsPage.enginesHint: Engine images are named by an index. Refresh re-reads it; the fields below decide which index, and how long its answer is kept.
settingsPage.defaultEngineHint: Used by a recipe that does not name one.
settingsPage.indexTtlHint: How long a fetched index is reused before it is read again.
settingsPage.sourcesHint: Where a model is downloaded from. A name here is what the download form and a recipe's source field select.
settingsPage.registriesHint: OCI registries that publish recipe collections. Browsing and installing one is on the Registries page; this is where they are added and turned on.
settingsPage.forgetRegistryBody: {name} is removed from the list. The collections already installed from it stay where they are.
settingsPage.autoUpdateHint: A background check for newer collection versions. It never applies an update to a recipe you have edited.
settingsPage.autoUpdateToggleHint: Run the check on the schedule below.
settingsPage.scheduleHint: A cron expression. Saved when the field loses focus, so a half-typed one is never the schedule.
settingsPage.mcpSameOrigin: This page is served by the backend, so {endpoint} is the same origin.
settingsPage.mcpDevServer: This page is the Vite dev server on port {devPort}; MCP lives on the backend, at {endpoint}.
settingsPage.mcpOffHint: This server started with MCP disabled.
settingsPage.mcpNotMountedBody: Nothing is listening at /mcp — a client pointed there would be refused. No endpoint is shown until it is turned back on.
settingsPage.apiTokenValue: mcp_api_token, sent as a bearer token
settingsPage.toolsHint: Asked of the endpoint itself, so this is what a client would see — not a list kept by hand here.
settingsPage.toolsFailed: Could not read the tool list from {endpoint}.
